section: Important things you should keep in mind about these benefits:
headers: You pay After the calendar year deductible…

rows.Benefits Description: • G.E.H.A needs to be notified of the first date of your dialysis, even when an extension is required for coordination of benefits. Refer to G.E.H.A's dialysis notification form located at geha.com/Dialysis-Notification. • See Section 5(f), Prescription drug benefits, for available medications required for treatment therapies.
rows.You pay After the calendar year deductib: In-network: 5% of the Plan allowance Out-of-network: 35% of the Plan allowance and any difference between our allowance and the billed amount

rows.Benefits Description: Not covered: • Chelation therapy except for acute arsenic, gold or lead poisoning • "Grocery" food items that can routinely be obtained online or in stores (e.g., gluten- free breads) • Maintenance cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation • Topical hyperbaric oxygen therapy • Prolotherapy • Ongoing licensed/unlicensed dialysis assistance in the home after initial dialysis training
Physical, occupational, speech, habilitative, and rehabilitative therapy

We cover up to 60 outpatient therapy visits per person per calendar year for the combined services when a physician: • orders the care; • identifies the specific professional skills the patient requires and the medical necessity for skilled services; and • indicates the length of time the services are needed. Notes: • Inpatient therapy services are not applied to the visit limits, see Section 5(c), Inpatient hospital • Rehabilitation and Habilitative therapy, see Section 10, Definitions of Terms
rows.You pay After the calendar year deductib: In-network: 5% of the Plan allowance Out-of-network: 35% of the Plan allowance and any difference between our allowance and the billed amount

rows.Benefits Description: Not covered: • Exercise programs • Long-term rehabilitative therapy • Maintenance therapy-measurable improvement is not expected, or progress is no longer demonstrated • Hot and cold packs • Hippotherapy • Rehabilitative services intended to teach or enhance Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (therapy to promote skills associated with independent living, such as shopping, using a phone, cleaning, laundry, preparing meals, managing medications, driving, or managing money/finances) • Sensory, Auditory, or Sensory Integration Therapy • Biofeedback, educational, recreational or milieu therapy
